title: Prusa MK4S Operator Badge
subtitle: Safe setup, first print, and quality checks

levels.title: Welcome to the Prusa MK4S
narrative: The Prusa MK4S is a reliable fused-filament 3D printer used for rapid prototyping and finished parts.
Before printing, always check the machine status, confirm the correct filament is loaded, and inspect the bed surface.
Your goal in this certification is to learn safe startup, first-layer quality checks, and basic troubleshooting.
callouts: Never start a print on a dirty build plate.
Do not leave the first layer unchecked.
Stop the machine if filament is tangled or the nozzle collides.
keyTakeaways: Check bed, filament, and slicer profile.

levels.title: Before You Press Print
levels.prompt: You are preparing a print on the MK4S. What is the best first action?
levels.situation: The bed has fingerprints on it, filament is loaded, and the print file is ready.

choices.label: Start the print immediately since the file is ready.
choices.feedback: Not quite. A dirty bed can cause first-layer adhesion problems.

choices.label: Clean the build plate before starting the print.
choices.feedback: Correct. Cleaning the build plate is one of the most important pre-print checks.

choices.label: Raise nozzle temperature first to improve adhesion.
choices.feedback: Temperature matters, but bed cleanliness is the priority in this situation.

levels.title: Spot the First-Layer Problems
levels.prompt: Tap the areas that would make you stop and inspect the print.
levels.imageAlt: First layer quality check on Prusa MK4S bed

hotspots.label: Lifted corner
hotspots.feedback: Correct. A lifted corner suggests poor bed adhesion.

hotspots.label: Visible gaps between lines
hotspots.feedback: Correct. Gaps in the first layer can indicate poor Z height or adhesion.

hotspots.label: Smooth, even layer area
hotspots.feedback: This area looks acceptable and would not be your first reason to stop.

questions.prompt: What should you do if the first layer is not sticking?

choices.label: Let it continue for a while and see if it fixes itself.
Stop the print, inspect the bed, and correct the issue.
Ignore it if only one corner is lifting.

questions.explanation: First-layer issues usually get worse, not better. Stop early and fix the cause.

questions.prompt: Which material is usually easiest for beginners to print on the Prusa MK4S?
questions.explanation: PLA is generally the best starting material because it is easier to print and troubleshoot.

levels.title: Ready to Run
levels.prompt: You cleaned the bed, loaded the right filament, sliced with the correct profile, and started the print. What should you do next?
levels.situation: The print has just started and the nozzle is laying down the first lines.

choices.label: Walk away immediately since the print file is known-good.
choices.feedback: Not yet. The first layer is the most important moment to observe.

choices.label: Watch the first layer for the first few minutes and confirm it is smooth and sticking well.
choices.feedback: Correct. Always watch the first layer before leaving the machine.

choices.label: Increase print speed right away to save time.
choices.feedback: That increases risk. Confirm a stable first layer before changing settings.
